nodes.label: Wildlife migration tracking

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Protected areas management|Wildlife migration tracking_qna_000
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How far did GPS tagged lapwings typically stay from their nests during the breeding period?
nodes.answer: GPS tagged lapwings stayed close to their nests throughout the breeding period, at an average distance of 207 153 m.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Protected areas management|Wildlife migration tracking_qna_001
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What data was recorded regarding the nests?
nodes.answer: The number and incubation stage of the eggs, as well as the exact location of the nest (averaged GPS coordinates) with a precision of approximately 3 m, were recorded.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Protected areas management|Wildlife migration tracking_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What equipment was used to track the Lapwings?
nodes.answer: GPS devices were equipped on the Lapwings at each of the seven study sites during the breeding seasons of 2022 and 2023.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Protected areas management|Wildlife migration tracking_qna_003
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: Why were certain individuals excluded from the study on habitat selection?
nodes.answer: Individuals were excluded if they failed reproduction and wandered away from the nest site, as well as three individuals due to GPS malfunctioning.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Protected areas management|Wildlife migration tracking_qna_004
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What percentage of the GPS tracking fixes fell within the nest buffer zone?
nodes.answer: The mean percentage of all GPS fixes that fell inside the nest buffer zone was 80.0% with a standard deviation of 17.3%.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Protected areas management|Wildlife migration tracking_qna_005
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What do weather radars detect besides weather?
nodes.answer: Weather radars also continuously register the movements of billions of animals aloft in the lower atmosphere.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Protected areas management|Wildlife migration tracking_qna_006
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What has contributed to the expansion of understanding aerial animal movements in Europe?
nodes.answer: The comprehensive datasets gathered from weather surveillance radars provide new avenues for understanding continental scale movements of aerial animals.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Protected areas management|Wildlife migration tracking_qna_007
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What are the two public datasets derived from European weather radars focused on?
nodes.answer: The datasets focus on animal movement data, particularly bird migration.
